html:
SMTO-GWT-0036 — That computer name can't be used

GUID: 20d0fe37-f555-41f5-88c2-6ec3fec38933
Slug: gateway-nickname-invalid
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • Each computer in SMTO needs its own short, readable name. The name given was empty, looked like a web or network address, or is already used by another computer, so it wasn't saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Edit on the computer (or Add Gateway for a new one) and type a plain name in Nickname, such as Office PC. The nickname is just the label you see, so it can't be left blank.
  2. Put the computer's network address only in the Host field. The nickname can't be a number address like 192.168.1.5, contain / ? or #, or start with http or www. SMTO refuses nicknames that look like addresses so they can't be mistaken for where to connect.
  3. Make sure no other computer in the list already has that name, even with different capital letters, and don't use LocalMachine. Then select Save changes. Two computers with the same name would make it unclear where your work runs, and LocalMachine is the built-in name for the SMTO server itself.

What success looks like

  • The dialog closes and the computer appears in the Gateways list under its new name.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep saving the same name; change it first, because it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway nickname validation rejected the label: it was blank, an IP address, URL-like (contains ://, /, ?, # or starts with http:, https:, www.), already used by another Gateway ignoring case, or no unique nickname could be generated.

What this means

  • Gateway label normalization rejected a blank, IP-like or URL-like nickname, or uniqueness checks found no unused label after case folding. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Gateway label normalization rejected a blank, IP-like or URL-like nickname, or uniqueness checks found no unused label after case folding.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the proposed nickname against existing labels and the rejected format; keep the endpoint in its host field.

How to fix it

  • Supply a non-empty, case-insensitively unique Gateway label that is not an IP address or URL-like (and not the reserved LocalMachine); keep the address in the Host/Port fields. If automatic seeding reports it cannot generate a unique nickname, rename conflicting Gateway records. Validation lives in gateways/store.py (_normalize_gateway_label, _ensure_unique_label).
  • Choose a distinct human-readable nickname for the intended Gateway. Keep its endpoint host in the separate endpoint configuration.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A distinct valid nickname is saved while the intended endpoint and identity remain intact.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
